key_decisions.ma_choice: FWFT: the head entry is visible on rd_data whenever empty is low, and rd_en pops it in the same cycle with zero read latency.
key_decisions.plan_choice: FWFT; rd_data shows the oldest entry while empty==0 and rd_en pops it in the same cycle.

key_decisions.ma_choice: Async-read register array (LUTRAM on FPGA, flop array plus mux on ASIC), recommended up to ~64 entries. A sync-read block RAM with a 1-entry prefetch register is deferred to a future MEM_STYLE parameter.
key_decisions.plan_choice: Same async-read register array, ~64 recommendation, and deferred MEM_STYLE block-RAM plus prefetch variant (via Q1).
key_decisions.note: Resolved through Q1, with the answer matching the MA.

key_decisions.ma_choice: rd_data driven combinationally from the async read mux indexed by the registered rd_ptr.
key_decisions.plan_choice: Combinational from the array mux driven by the registered rd_ptr; no path from rd_en to rd_data.

key_decisions.ma_choice: Power-of-two DEPTH (2..65536) checked at elaboration; pointers ADDR_W+1 bits with a wrap MSB.
key_decisions.plan_choice: Power-of-two only, minimum 2, upper bound 65536, elaboration assertion, log2(DEPTH)+1-bit pointers with wrap bit.

key_decisions.ma_choice: Registered full/empty/almost_full/level, all computed from level_n (next-state level). Pointer-derived full/empty kept only as an assertion cross-check.
key_decisions.plan_choice: Registered full, empty and count computed from next-state values; almost_full registered as count_next >= af_thresh.
key_decisions.note: The plan does not mention the pointer-based assertion cross-check, but the architecture is identical.

key_decisions.ma_choice: Runtime input port af_thresh of width ADDR_W+1, quasi-static. almost_full = level >= af_thresh; thresh 0 means always on, > DEPTH means never.
key_decisions.plan_choice: Runtime af_thresh port of width log2(DEPTH)+1 with almost_full = count >= af_thresh. Threshold edge cases 0 and > DEPTH and runtime-change behaviour (one-cycle lag) are covered.

key_decisions.ma_choice: level output of width ADDR_W+1 (0..DEPTH), also used to derive the flags.
key_decisions.plan_choice: count output of width log2(DEPTH)+1, also used internally for almost_full.

key_decisions.ma_choice: Both accepted: wr_fire = wr_en && (!full_q || rd_fire). No overflow is flagged, and there is an internal combinational rd_en-to-write-enable path.
key_decisions.plan_choice: Both accepted with wr_accept = wr_en && (!full || rd_en); no overflow; the rd_en-to-wr_accept path is noted as critical.

key_decisions.ma_choice: No bypass. Only the write is accepted, the read sets underflow, and data is visible the next cycle.
key_decisions.plan_choice: No bypass; write accepted, read ignored and flags underflow, data visible next cycle (via Q2).

key_decisions.ma_choice: overflow on wr_en && !wr_fire; underflow on rd_en && !rd_fire.
key_decisions.plan_choice: overflow on wr_en && !wr_accept; underflow on rd_en && empty_q.
key_decisions.note: The two underflow expressions are equivalent.

key_decisions.decision: Sticky error clear mechanism and priority
key_decisions.ma_choice: Single shared err_clr pulse clears both flags; err_clr wins over a same-cycle new error (to be confirmed with SW); no internal register interface.
key_decisions.plan_choice: Single shared err_clr pulse; clear wins; no register interface; priority marked as to be confirmed (via Q3).

key_decisions.ma_choice: Active-low rst_n, asynchronous assert and synchronous deassert from an external synchronizer. Control flops are reset (empty=1); mem is not reset.
key_decisions.plan_choice: Async-assert active-low rst_n on control flops, deassertion synchronised upstream, memory array not reset.
key_decisions.note: The spec fixes only the polarity.

key_decisions.ma_choice: 1 read and 1 write per cycle sustained. Critical paths are rd_ptr→read mux→rd_data and level→adder→compare→flag.
key_decisions.plan_choice: 1 word/cycle each direction. Critical paths listed as rd_en→wr_accept→write enable and rd_ptr→mux→rd_data.
key_decisions.note: The plan omits the level adder/compare path but adds the rd_en→wr_accept path. The overall characterization is consistent.

summary: The plan matches the reference MA on essentially every architecture-level decision: FWFT with an async-read register array and a deferred MEM_STYLE block-RAM variant, power-of-two DEPTH with wrap-bit pointers, registered flags from next-state level, a runtime af_thresh port, accept-both at full, no bypass at empty, a shared err_clr with clear priority, and async-assert reset with unreset memory. All three questions targeted genuinely open points the spec left ambiguous (memory style for deep FIFOs, read+write at empty, clear mechanism), so none were needless. The answers align exactly with the MA. Only trivial omissions exist, such as the pointer-based assertion cross-check.
